contentBlocks.text: This week you mastered exponential functions four ways. Let's review it all!

Quick review: y=a·bˣ, with b>1 for growth and 0<b<1 for decay (Day 1). Its graph has a y-intercept at (0,a) and a horizontal asymptote at y=0 (Day 2). You modeled compound interest growth (Day 3) and radioactive decay (Day 4). A $500 deposit grows at 8% annual interest. Find the balance after 2 years, and explain whether this is growth or decay and why.
Great work this week — you mastered exponential functions and applied them to real growth and decay problems! Next week we'll build on these skills with something new.

objectives: Review exponential functions, their graphs, and real-world growth/decay applications
Correctly calculate the 8%-interest balance and explain why it's growth
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Do the quick walk-through review of all 4 days together, out loud.
2. Have the child solve the new compound interest problem and explain growth vs. decay.
3. Complete the review worksheet.
4. Celebrate finishing a full week of exponential-function mastery!
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just the skill the child found hardest this week (often distinguishing growth vs. decay) rather than requiring all four equally
Ready for more: ask the child how this week's exponential functions differ from last week's quadratic functions in their overall shape and behavior
This is a good checkpoint to note which of the week's four exponential-function skills needs the most reinforcement going forward
teacherGuide.answerKey: A = 500(1.08)² = 500 × 1.1664 = $583.20. This is growth, since the growth factor b=1.08 is greater than 1, matching the compound-interest pattern from Day 3.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Consolidates this week's Common Core Algebra 2 exponential-function standards (F-LE.1/F-LE.2/F-IF.7e) before the course continues, matching the established Day-5-review pacing used across every unit this session.
